passages.label: Evaluate AI automation and voice agents for your business — Evaluate AI automation and voice agents for your business
passages.passage: Choose an AI automation project by finding a repeated task with clear inputs, an approved response, and a person who can handle exceptions. For voice agents, start with a narrow inbound workflow and test it against realistic calls. Decide what success means before expanding access or allowing actions without review.
passages.title: Evaluate AI automation and voice agents for your business
passages.heading: Evaluate AI automation and voice agents for your business

passages.label: Evaluate AI automation and voice agents for your business — Choose a bounded first job
passages.passage: Consider appointment intake, routing a common enquiry, or drafting a follow-up for staff review. Write down what the system may answer and what it must pass to a person. Treat an impressive demonstration as the start of evaluation, not proof that it will handle your entire business.
passages.title: Evaluate AI automation and voice agents for your business
passages.heading: Choose a bounded first job

passages.label: What should I check before connecting an AI agent to my CRM? — What should I check before connecting an AI agent to my CRM?
passages.passage: Define exactly which CRM records the agent may read, create, or update before connecting it. Use limited access and test with non-production records. Require review for sensitive changes and verify how duplicates, failures, and retries are handled. Assign a person to monitor the integration and revoke access when it is no longer needed.
passages.title: What should I check before connecting an AI agent to my CRM?
passages.heading: What should I check before connecting an AI agent to my CRM?

passages.label: What should I check before connecting an AI agent to my CRM? — Specify permitted actions
passages.passage: List the required fields and operations for the pilot. Distinguish drafting a note from changing a customer record or triggering outreach. Ask the provider to demonstrate the proposed permission settings and the record of changes, instead of granting broad access to simplify setup.
passages.title: What should I check before connecting an AI agent to my CRM?
passages.heading: Specify permitted actions

passages.label: When should an AI voice agent transfer to a person? — When should an AI voice agent transfer to a person?
passages.passage: Define handoff rules before launch: a caller asks for a person, the agent lacks an approved answer, a required system is unavailable, or the conversation involves an exception outside its authority. Test the transfer and the fallback if nobody answers. Staff should receive enough context to continue without making the caller start over.
passages.title: When should an AI voice agent transfer to a person?
passages.heading: When should an AI voice agent transfer to a person?

passages.label: When should an AI voice agent transfer to a person? — Write the boundary in plain language
passages.passage: List what the agent may confirm, what it may only collect for review, and what it must escalate. Include disputes, requests to change account access, unusual scheduling needs, and any question your team considers sensitive. Do not leave the escalation decision entirely to a vague instruction to be helpful.
passages.title: When should an AI voice agent transfer to a person?
passages.heading: Write the boundary in plain language

passages.label: Does AI search need different SEO or special markup? — Does AI search need different SEO or special markup?
passages.passage: Google says its established SEO practices also apply to AI Overviews and AI Mode, with no special schema or AI text file required. Pages must be indexed and eligible for a search snippet to appear as supporting links. Prioritize accessible content, helpful answers, internal links, and accurate structured data without promising AI placement.
passages.title: Does AI search need different SEO or special markup?
passages.heading: Does AI search need different SEO or special markup?

passages.label: Does AI search need different SEO or special markup? — Keep the basics verifiable
passages.passage: Google recommends allowing crawling, making important information available as text, using internal links, and matching structured data to what visitors can see. Ask for evidence that your actual pages meet these conditions before buying a package built around a new acronym.
passages.title: Does AI search need different SEO or special markup?
passages.heading: Keep the basics verifiable

passages.label: Do AI voice agents work for service businesses? — Do AI voice agents work for service businesses?
passages.passage: An AI voice agent is worth evaluating for a defined task such as inbound intake or appointment routing, but suitability depends on your calls and integrations. Test realistic conversations, exceptions, and human handoff before relying on it. Judge the pilot by accurate completed tasks and staff corrections, not by how natural one demonstration sounds.
passages.title: Do AI voice agents work for service businesses?
passages.heading: Do AI voice agents work for service businesses?

passages.label: Do AI voice agents work for service businesses? — Start with your actual calls
passages.passage: Write a list of common enquiry types and decide which the pilot may handle. Include callers who interrupt, change their minds, spell unfamiliar names, or ask for a person. Test what happens when the agent cannot find an answer or reach the scheduling system.
passages.title: Do AI voice agents work for service businesses?
passages.heading: Start with your actual calls

passages.label: Should a local business use an AI-built website? — Should a local business use an AI-built website?
passages.passage: A local business can consider an AI-built website when the finished site accurately explains its services and makes it easy for customers to enquire. Judge the result by content accuracy, mobile usability, ownership, and maintenance. Have a person verify every business claim and test the contact or booking path before launch.
passages.title: Should a local business use an AI-built website?
passages.heading: Should a local business use an AI-built website?

passages.label: Should a local business use an AI-built website? — Use a launch checklist
passages.passage: Evaluate the finished website against the same requirements you would give any website provider. Verify services, service areas, hours, and contact details. Remove invented reviews, results, and business claims. Test contact and booking on a phone. Confirm domain, hosting, file ownership, and ongoing editing access.
passages.title: Should a local business use an AI-built website?
passages.heading: Use a launch checklist

passages.label: Choose a website around the next customer decision — Choose a website around the next customer decision
passages.passage: Start a business website project by deciding what a visitor needs to understand and do: request an estimate, book a visit, or buy. Then define the pages, content, integrations, ownership, and maintenance. Ask for a written scope and a working demonstration of the enquiry path before approving launch.
passages.title: Choose a website around the next customer decision
passages.heading: Choose a website around the next customer decision

passages.label: Choose a website around the next customer decision — Write the brief before comparing proposals
passages.passage: List the services you actually deliver, the customers you serve, the questions your team answers, and the evidence you can publish. Ask each vendor to price the same scope. Specify who writes the copy, supplies images, approves revisions, and maintains the site. Keep optional integrations separate so you can decide what to build first.
passages.title: Choose a website around the next customer decision
passages.heading: Write the brief before comparing proposals

passages.label: California: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules — California: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
passages.passage: Short answer: California’s SB 478 generally requires advertised consumer prices to include mandatory fees. The Attorney General says an avoidable credit-card fee generally is not mandatory, but a fee is mandatory when a business only accepts credit cards. Dual pricing and surcharging still need separate review under applicable laws and card-network rules. Not legal advice. This is general information from the linked sources, reviewed October 28, 2026. Laws and network rules can change. Have your legal adviser and acquirer review your actual pricing, locations, and checkout before implementation.
passages.title: California: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
passages.heading: California: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules

passages.label: California: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules — The payment options change the advertised-price analysis
passages.passage: SB 478 took effect July 1, 2024. California’s DOJ FAQ says a card processing fee generally is not mandatory when the customer can avoid it by paying another way, such as cash. If credit cards are the only accepted payment method, the fee must be included in the advertised price. Do not describe SB 478 as a blanket ban on all surcharges.
passages.title: California: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
passages.heading: The payment options change the advertised-price analysis

passages.label: How does a cash discount program work for a restaurant? — How does a cash discount program work for a restaurant?
passages.passage: A restaurant cash discount program gives customers a lower price when they pay cash instead of the displayed card price. Dual pricing shows both prices before payment. Review menus, signs, checkout screens, and receipts together, then have your provider review the setup for your locations before training staff or changing prices. Not legal advice. This is general information from the linked sources, reviewed October 28, 2026. Laws and network rules can change. Have your legal adviser and acquirer review your actual pricing, locations, and checkout before implementation.
passages.title: How does a cash discount program work for a restaurant?
passages.heading: How does a cash discount program work for a restaurant?

passages.label: How does a cash discount program work for a restaurant? — Start with a restaurant checklist
passages.passage: Bring the customer’s complete ordering and payment path to the review. List dine-in, takeout, online ordering, and telephone payments. Check the prices on menus, signs, and checkout screens. Ask for demonstrations of cash, credit, debit, tips, and refunds. Request the full processing, gateway, and equipment proposal.
passages.title: How does a cash discount program work for a restaurant?
passages.heading: Start with a restaurant checklist

passages.label: How do I get my business recommended by ChatGPT? — How do I get my business recommended by ChatGPT?
passages.passage: There is no guaranteed way to make ChatGPT recommend a business. Publish clear, accurate information about your services and make it accessible to search crawlers. OpenAI identifies OAI-SearchBot as its search crawler and says placement is not guaranteed. Focus on useful answers and credible evidence rather than promises of a paid or automatic recommendation.
passages.title: How do I get my business recommended by ChatGPT?
passages.heading: How do I get my business recommended by ChatGPT?

passages.label: How do I get my business recommended by ChatGPT? — Make the business understandable
passages.passage: Explain what you do, who you serve, where you operate, and how customers can contact you. Answer the decisions buyers face and cite sources for claims. This is an editorial approach to useful content, not a documented formula for getting selected in an AI response.
passages.title: How do I get my business recommended by ChatGPT?
passages.heading: Make the business understandable

passages.label: What does a merchant services consultant do, and how do I choose one? — What does a merchant services consultant do, and how do I choose one?
passages.passage: A merchant services consultant helps you review payment costs, compare proposals, and match processing to how your business takes payments. Choose one who reviews your statement, explains every cost component, and demonstrates the proposed workflow. Ask for written terms, clear support responsibilities, and a migration plan before agreeing to change providers.
passages.title: What does a merchant services consultant do, and how do I choose one?
passages.heading: What does a merchant services consultant do, and how do I choose one?

passages.label: What does a merchant services consultant do, and how do I choose one? — Use a short selection checklist
passages.passage: Give each consultant the same business requirements so their proposals can be compared. Request a statement review and a complete written proposal. Separate processing, gateway, software, and equipment costs. Ask who handles support and account changes. Confirm cancellation, data access, and migration responsibilities.
passages.title: What does a merchant services consultant do, and how do I choose one?
passages.heading: Use a short selection checklist

passages.label: Colorado: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules — Colorado: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
passages.passage: Short answer: Colorado’s enacted SB21-091 permits a credit-card surcharge within a framework of 2% of the transaction or the actual merchant discount fee. It requires notice and excludes debit, cash, check, and gift-card payments. Card-network limits still apply. Have the acquirer document the permitted calculation and presentation for your proposed setup. Not legal advice. This is general information from the linked sources, reviewed October 28, 2026. Laws and network rules can change. Have your legal adviser and acquirer review your actual pricing, locations, and checkout before implementation.
passages.title: Colorado: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
passages.heading: Colorado: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules

passages.label: Colorado: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules — Do not flatten the rule into one universal cap
passages.passage: The enacted summary describes a limit of 2% of the transaction or the merchant discount fee, defined as the actual fee paid to process it. It does not support describing Colorado as an unconditional permission to pass through any amount. Ask for review of the chosen calculation and supporting records.
passages.title: Colorado: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
passages.heading: Do not flatten the rule into one universal cap

passages.label: Connecticut: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules — Connecticut: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
passages.passage: Short answer: Connecticut prohibits businesses from adding a surcharge for one payment method over another, while allowing genuine cash discounts. Its consumer agency identifies posting both cash and card prices as a compliant approach. An added transaction fee or non-cash adjustment can still be a prohibited surcharge. Review the actual prices and receipts before launch. Not legal advice. This is general information from the linked sources, reviewed October 28, 2026. Laws and network rules can change. Have your legal adviser and acquirer review your actual pricing, locations, and checkout before implementation.
passages.title: Connecticut: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
passages.heading: Connecticut: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules

passages.label: Connecticut: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules — A different name does not change an added fee
passages.passage: Connecticut DCP cites §42-133ff and its amendment by Public Act 24-142. It explains that adding a processing fee, transaction fee, or non-cash adjustment to the listed price is a surcharge. Start the review with the displayed price, not the terminal vendor’s program label.
passages.title: Connecticut: dual pricing and credit-card surcharge rules
passages.heading: A different name does not change an added fee

passages.label: Is dual pricing legal? — Is dual pricing legal?
passages.passage: Dual pricing can be lawful when the displayed cash and card prices, checkout behavior, and receipts follow applicable law and card rules. It is not a universal exemption from surcharge restrictions. A fee added to a posted price may be a surcharge regardless of its name. Review each location before implementation. Not legal advice. This is general information from the linked sources, reviewed October 28, 2026. Laws and network rules can change. Have your legal adviser and acquirer review your actual pricing, locations, and checkout before implementation.
passages.title: Is dual pricing legal?
passages.heading: Is dual pricing legal?

passages.label: Is dual pricing legal? — Follow the money and the displayed price
passages.passage: Visa describes a genuine cash discount as a reduction from the displayed card price, or from card and cash prices shown side by side. Adding a fee at checkout to reach the card price can be treated as a surcharge. Review the shelf label, online product page, invoice, and receipt together.
passages.title: Is dual pricing legal?
passages.heading: Follow the money and the displayed price

passages.label: What is an embedded checkout? — What is an embedded checkout?
passages.passage: An embedded checkout places a provider’s payment form inside your website so customers can enter payment details without leaving that page. A hosted checkout redirects to a provider page. Choose between them by reviewing supported payment methods, mobile behavior, maintenance, and your order workflow, then test both successful and failed payments.
passages.title: What is an embedded checkout?
passages.heading: What is an embedded checkout?

passages.label: What is an embedded checkout? — Match the checkout to the purchase
passages.passage: Stripe documents hosted and embedded options, with different customization and maintenance characteristics. Use those categories to frame your requirements, not to assume every provider has identical features. Request a demonstration of the specific checkout proposed for your website and payment account.
passages.title: What is an embedded checkout?
passages.heading: Match the checkout to the purchase

passages.label: Will FAQ schema get my business rich results or AI citations? — Will FAQ schema get my business rich results or AI citations?
passages.passage: FAQ schema describes visible questions and answers, but it does not guarantee a rich result or an AI citation. Google currently limits FAQ rich results to well-known authoritative government and health websites. A business should use accurate markup that matches its page and focus on genuinely useful answers rather than a promised search enhancement.
passages.title: Will FAQ schema get my business rich results or AI citations?
passages.heading: Will FAQ schema get my business rich results or AI citations?

passages.label: Will FAQ schema get my business rich results or AI citations? — Keep markup consistent with the page
passages.passage: Google’s FAQ guidance requires that the marked-up questions and answers be visible to visitors. Use the same content source for the displayed FAQ and JSON-LD so later edits cannot leave contradictory answers. Do not add claims to schema that are absent from the page.
passages.title: Will FAQ schema get my business rich results or AI citations?
passages.heading: Keep markup consistent with the page

passages.label: What should a small business automate first? — What should a small business automate first?
passages.passage: Start with a repeated task that has a clear trigger, a predictable outcome, and an easy way for staff to catch mistakes. Map the current process before choosing software. Keep the first pilot narrow, assign an owner, and compare completed work and correction time before deciding whether to expand it.
passages.title: What should a small business automate first?
passages.heading: What should a small business automate first?

passages.label: What should a small business automate first? — Describe the task without naming a tool
passages.passage: Write down the trigger, input, decision, action, and exception path. A useful candidate might be routing an enquiry for review or preparing a draft response from approved information. Exclude tasks whose rules your team cannot yet explain consistently.
passages.title: What should a small business automate first?
passages.heading: Describe the task without naming a tool

passages.label: How do I rank in Google’s map pack? — How do I rank in Google’s map pack?
